rv.q: They deliver three hours of drama, a winding tale of madness and thwarted love in the English Civil War, with agile bravura, graceful sensitivity and, of course, beautiful singing.
As long as you ignore Edwards’s sometimes puzzling stage imagery, this I Puritani delivers vocal sizzle aplenty.
For the Met's first performance since 2017, and the 64th in the company's 142-year history, it has assembled an inspired cast.
On Wednesday’s opening night, Oropesa and Brownlee were both excellent.

cn.t: Critics praise the Met's new production of Bellini's bel canto masterpiece, with particular acclaim for the gorgeous melodies and stellar vocal performances from Lisette Oropesa and Lawrence Brownlee.
